check.negative: The template prints nothing at all, so the expected text is absent and the check fails. There is no accidental pass here: an empty run cannot contain the string.

en: There is no printf in HolyC and no function call needed. A string on its own, as a statement, prints itself. Open /Doc/HelloWorld.DD - it is one line long.

Write the string followed by a semicolon, exactly as if it were a statement:  "Hello, World
";  The 
 at the end starts a new line.
Full solution with a line-by-line walkthrough - see Solution.HC. Looking costs you nothing except the one campaign-wide achievement for never looking.
ru: В HolyC нет printf, и вызывать ничего не нужно. Строка сама по себе, как оператор, печатает себя. Откройте /Doc/HelloWorld.DD — он длиной в одну строку.

Напишите строку и точку с запятой, как обычный оператор:  "Hello, World
";  Символ 
 в конце переводит строку.
Полное решение с построчным разбором — см. Solution.HC. Просмотр ничего не стоит, кроме единственной ачивки за прохождение кампании без подсказок.

_notes: The first task where the answer is not a function. It exists to land one idea: in HolyC the shell is the compiler, and a bare expression is a statement that runs.
Checked by capturing output rather than by calling anything, which is why the stdout check kind had to exist before this task could.
